background_notes.fact: For continuous Hilbert-space-valued G on a compact interval [c,d], ||integral_c^d G(s) ds|| <= (d-c) sup_[c,d]||G(s)||. If F(t)=integral_c^t G(s) ds, then F'=G on the interval interior. These facts also apply separately on each smooth piece.

background_notes.justification: The integral norm inequality follows by applying the triangle inequality to Riemann sums and passing to their norm limit. The difference quotient for F is the average of G on a shrinking interval and converges to G(t) by norm continuity.
